322976.title: The chromatic bound conjecture for additive coloring
322976.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. Write $\chi(G)$ for its chromatic number and let $\eta(G)$ be the least number of labels in an additive coloring of $G$.

**Chromatic bound conjecture.** Every graph $G$ satisfies

$$
\eta(G)\leqslant \chi(G).
$$

It is not known whether this holds even for bipartite graphs; it is not known whether $\eta(G)$ is bounded on bipartite graphs. The conjecture is trivial if arbitrary real labels are allowed, but the finite-label version remains open.

323179.title: Diagonal uniqueness conjecture for Sprague–Grundy values of F-Wythoff
323179.statement:
Let $\mathcal{G}(x,y)$ be the Sprague–Grundy value of the position $(x,y)$ in $\mathcal{F}$-Wythoff. For nonnegative integers $a$ and $g$, consider the diagonal parallel to the main diagonal given by positions $(b,a+b)$.

**Diagonal uniqueness conjecture.** For all nonnegative integers $a$ and $g$, there exists a unique integer $b$ such that

$$
\mathcal{G}(b,a+b)=g.
$$

For ordinary Wythoff's game, every such diagonal contains every nonnegative Sprague–Grundy value. The conjecture asserts the corresponding existence and uniqueness for $\mathcal{F}$-Wythoff; the source presents it as a conjecture based on computer explorations.

325227.title: Aalipour-Hafshejani et al.'s domination-polynomial uniqueness conjecture for complete bipartite graphs
325227.statement:
Let $a,b\in\mathbb{N}$, and let ${\cal K}(a,b)$ denote the complete bipartite graph with parts of sizes $a$ and $b$. Two graphs are **${\cal D}$-equivalent** when they have the same domination polynomial.

**Aalipour-Hafshejani et al.'s conjecture.** For all $a,b\in\mathbb{N}$, if $|a-b|\geq 2$, then ${\cal K}(a,b)$ is ${\cal D}$-unique; that is, every graph with the same domination polynomial as ${\cal K}(a,b)$ is isomorphic to it.

This conjecture concerns whether complete bipartite graphs with unequal parts differing by at least two are determined by their domination polynomial. The paper states that its results settle the conjecture affirmatively: any two such complete bipartite graphs with the same domination polynomial are isomorphic.

325320.title: Moment lower-bound conjecture for bootstrap percolation on Galton–Watson trees
325320.statement:
Let $T_\xi$ be a Galton–Watson tree with offspring distribution $\xi$. **Moment lower-bound conjecture.** For every $r\geq 2$ and $\alpha\in(0,r-1]$, there exists a constant $c_{r,\alpha}>0$ such that

$$
p_c(T_\xi,r)\geq c_{r,\alpha}\left({\mathbb E}(\xi^{1+\alpha})\right)^{-1/\alpha}.
$$

This extends the previously established moment lower bound from $\alpha\in(0,1]$ to all $\alpha\leq r-1$; the source gives no resolution.

326292.title: Manickam–Miklós–Singhi conjecture for sets
326292.statement:
Let $n$ real numbers $w_1,\u2026,w_n$ satisfy

$$
w_1+cdots+w_n\geq 0.
$$

A $k$-subset $A$ is **nonnegative** when $sum_{w_i\in A}w_i\geq 0$. **Manickam–Mikl\f3sSinghi conjecture.** If $n\geq 4k$, then at least

$$
\binom{n-1}{k-1}
$$

of the $k$-subsets $A$ are nonnegative. This is the classical MMS problem on nonnegative $k$-sums; the paper's abstract notes that it is verified for the range $n>10k^3$, while the conjecture asserts the bound for all $n\geq 4k$.

326437.title: Ma et al.'s signature bounds conjecture for simple graphs
326437.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple graph with adjacency matrix $A(G)$. Its **signature** is $s(G)=p(G)-n(G)$, where $p(G)$ and $n(G)$ are respectively the numbers of positive and negative eigenvalues of $A(G)$. Let $c_3(G)$ and $c_5(G)$ denote respectively the numbers of cycles in $G$ whose lengths are $4k+3$ and $4k+5$ for some integers $k\geq 0$. **Ma et al.'s signature bounds conjecture.** The inequality

$$
-c_3(G)\leq s(G)\leq c_5(G)
$$

possibly holds for every simple graph $G$. Ma et al. proved the inequality for trees, unicyclic graphs, and bicyclic graphs. This paper proves it for line graphs and power trees, while the general case is not established here.

327233.title: Hivert–Mallet–Mallet vectorial conjecture for irreducible k-shapes and surjective pistols
327233.statement: For $k\geq 3$, let $IS_k$ be the set of irreducible $k$-shapes. For an irreducible $k$-shape $\lambda$, let $\overrightarrow{fr}(\lambda)=(t_1,\ldots,t_{k-2})\in\{0,1\}^{k-2}$ record its free $k$-sites. Let $SP_{k-1}$ be the set of surjective pistols, and for $f\in SP_{k-1}$ let $\overrightarrow{fix}(f)=(t_1,\ldots,t_{k-2})\in\{0,1\}^{k-2}$, where $t_i=1$ exactly when $f(2i)=2i$. **Mallet's vectorial conjecture.** For every $k\geq 3$ and every $\overrightarrow{v}=(v_1,\ldots,v_{k-2})\in\{0,1\}^{k-2}$, the number of $\lambda\in IS_k$ with $\overrightarrow{fr}(\lambda)=\overrightarrow{v}$ equals the number of $f\in SP_{k-1}$ with $\overrightarrow{fix}(f)=\overrightarrow{v}$. This refines the corresponding equality of generating functions by preserving the full statistic vector.

328307.title: The sequential decomposition conjecture for graph orientations
328307.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. A **sequential decomposition** of a digraph $J$ is an ordered sequence of spanning subdigraphs $H_1,H_2,\ldots$ such that every arc of $J$ belongs to exactly one $H_i$. **The sequential decomposition conjecture.** There is an orientation $J$ of $G$ with no directed odd cycle and a sequential decomposition $H_1,H_2,\ldots$ such that each component of $H_i$ is a directed path or directed even cycle, and

$$
d^+_{H_i}(v)\geq d^+_{H_{i+1}}(v)
$$

for every $v\in V(J)$ and every $i$.

The conjecture is presented as a graph-decomposition statement implying the preceding $k$-optimal set conjecture, and hence the corresponding special case of Tuza's conjecture. Its resolution is not supplied in the source.

328610.title: Lu–Milans bounded Lubell function conjecture for induced-free families
328610.statement:
Let $P$ be a finite poset, let $n$ be a positive integer, and let $\mathcal{F}\subseteq 2^{[n]}$. Define its **Lubell function** by

$$
\lambda(\mathcal{F})=\sum_{F\in\mathcal{F}}\frac{1}{\binom{n}{\lvert F\rvert}}.
$$

**Lu–Milans conjecture.** For every poset $P$, there is a constant $C$ such that every induced $P$-free family $\mathcal{F}$ satisfies

$$
\sum_{F\in\mathcal{F}}\frac{1}{\binom{n}{\lvert F\rvert}}\leq C.
$$

This strengthens the preceding conjecture by bounding the Lubell function rather than merely the family size. The source says that the authors could not establish it and gives only a weaker shifted Lubell-function estimate.

328750.title: The alternating sign property for the matching derangement graph
328750.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be the matching derangement graph. For a partition $\lambda\vdash n$, define its **depth** by $d(\lambda)=n-\lambda_1$, and let $\eta_\lambda$ be an eigenvalue of $\Gamma$ indexed by $\lambda$. **The alternating sign property for the matching derangement graph.** For every partition $\lambda\vdash n$, 
$$
\operatorname{sign}(\eta_\lambda)=(-1)^{d(\lambda)}.
$$
 The property was verified computationally for $n<8$ and is proposed as a likely extension of the alternating sign property known for the permutation derangement graph; its general validity remains open.

328890.title: The inverse sieve conjecture
328890.statement:
Let $X\subset [N]$ be a subset and let $epsilon>0$ be real. Assume that for every real parameter $Q\geq N^{\epsilon}$,

$$
\sum_{p\leq Q}\frac{|X\pmod p|}{p}\leq (1-\epsilon)\pi(Q).
$$

**Inverse sieve conjecture.** At least one of the following holds: $|X|\ll_{\epsilon}N^{\epsilon}$, or there exists a polynomial $f(x)\in\mathbb{Q}[x]$ of degree $d\in[2,C]$ and height at most $N^C$ such that $|X\cap f([N])|\geq C^{-1}|X|$, where $C=C(\epsilon)$ is a constant. This conjecture predicts that a set occupying substantially fewer than the available residue classes on average is either very small or has a substantial intersection with a bounded-complexity polynomial value set; it is used in the paper to obtain an improved larger-sieve bound.

329072.title: Folklore clique-decomposition conjecture for complete graphs
329072.statement:
For a graph $G$, being **$K_{r+1}$-divisible** means that the necessary divisibility conditions for a $K_{r+1}$-decomposition hold. **Folklore clique-decomposition conjecture.** For every $r \in \mathbb{N}$ with $r \geq 2$, there exists an $n_0=n_0(r)$ such that every $K_{r+1}$-divisible graph $G$ on $n \geq n_0$ vertices with

$$
\delta(G) \geq (1-1/(r+2))n
$$

has a $K_{r+1}$-decomposition. This is presented as a natural extension of Nash-Williams' conjecture, with the corresponding extremal construction described in the paper; its resolution is not stated in the supplied text.

330692.title: Signed-shift allowed-pattern inequality conjecture
330692.statement:
Let $\mathcal A_n(\Sigma_k)$ and $\mathcal A_n(\Sigma^-_k)$ denote the sets of allowed patterns of length $n$ for the shifts $\Sigma_k$ and $\Sigma^-_k$, respectively. **Allowed-pattern inequality conjecture.** For $n\geq 3$, one has

$$
|\mathcal A_n(\Sigma_k)|\leq |\mathcal A_n(\Sigma^-_k)|.
$$

This conjectures that, for every shift parameter $k$ and pattern length at least three, the signed shift has at least as many allowed patterns as the corresponding unsigned shift. It generalizes the preceding result for $k=2$, where the inequality is strict for $n\geq 4$ and equality holds for $n\leq 3$; the proposed generalization is based on numerical evidence.

330859.title: Permutation lower-bound conjecture for partial Sylvester sums
330859.statement:
Let $(e_i)$ be the natural basis of $l_1$, let $\cal S^{(n)}=[s_{ki}^{(n)}]$ be the Sylvester matrix of order $2^n$, and define

$$
a_k=\sum_{i=1}^{2^n}s_{ki}^{(n)}e_i,
$$

for $k=1,\ldots,2^n$. Set

$$
m_n=\frac{2^{n+1}+(-1)^n}{3}.
$$

For a permutation $\sigma$ of ${1,2,\ldots,2^n}$, consider the sum of the first $m_n$ permuted vectors.

**Permutation lower-bound conjecture.** For every positive integer $n$ and every permutation $\sigma:\{1,2,\ldots,2^n\}\to\{1,2,\ldots,2^n\}$,

$$
\left\Vert\sum_{k=1}^{m_n}a_{\sigma(k)}\right\Vert_{l_1}\ge\frac{(3n+7)2^n}{9}+\frac{2(-1)^n}{9}.
$$

The paper gives a universal upper bound of $2^{3n/2}$ for these permuted partial sums but states that the authors do not know whether this lower bound holds. Thus the conjecture remains open.

330904.title: Xia's divisibility conjecture for 3-core partition triples
330904.statement:
Let $A_{3}(n)$ denote the number of partition triples of $n$ whose components are 3-cores. For a positive integer $j$ and a prime $p$, consider the values of $A_{3}(n)$ in the arithmetic progressions below. **Xia's conjecture.** For any positive integer $j$ and prime $p$, there exists a positive integer $k_{0}$ such that for all $n\ge 0$ and $\alpha \ge 0$, 

$$
A_{3}\Big(4^{k_{0}(\alpha+1)}n+\frac{2^{2k_{0}(\alpha+1)-1}-2}{3}\Big) \equiv 0 \pmod{p^{j}}.
$$

This conjecture proposes arbitrarily prescribed prime-power divisibility for an infinite family of values of $A_{3}(n)$, extending known congruences modulo $4$ and $8$ for 3-core partition triples.

331559.title: Shi's conjecture on UPC graphs with at least four extra edges
331559.statement: Let a UPC graph be a graph that is $(r)$-pancyclic for every positive integer $r$ in the relevant range, and let $v$ be its number of vertices and $v+m$ its number of edges. **Shi's conjecture.** There is no UPC graph with $v$ vertices and $v+m$ edges for $m\geq 4$. This conjecture extends Shi's classification of UPC graphs with $v+m$ edges for $m=0,1,2,3$; the source reports the assertion but gives no resolution.

331859.title: The decomposed-spider conjecture for graph burning
331859.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree containing a **decomposed spider** formed by paths $\\{Q_i\\}_{i=1}^t$, where $t\geq 3$, and let $v_i$ be the non-terminal endpoint of $Q_i$ for $1\leq i\leq t$. Write $b(G)$ for the burning number of a graph $G$. 

**Decomposed-spider conjecture.** If

$$
b\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^t Q_i\right)\geq k
$$

and

$$
d(v_i,v_j)\geq 2k
$$

for all $1\leq i,j\leq t$, then $b(T)\geq k+1$.

This conjecture proposes that a sufficiently separated decomposed spider forces the ambient tree to require at least one more burning step than the spider itself. The supplied text gives no resolution evidence, so its status is left open.

333080.title: Stein's equitable perfect matching conjecture
333080.statement:
Let $K_{n,n}$ be the complete bipartite graph with $n$ vertices in each part, and suppose its edges are partitioned into sets $E_1,\ldots,E_m$, where $m\leqslant n$. A **perfect matching** is a matching containing one edge incident with every vertex. **Stein's equitable perfect matching conjecture.** There exists a perfect matching $F$ in $K_{n,n}$ such that

$$
|F\cap E_i|\geqslant\left\lfloor\frac{|E_i|}{n}\right\rfloor-1
$$

for every $i$, with strict inequality holding for all but one value of $i$. This conjecture is implied by Stein's rainbow matching conjecture and is known in the case $m=3$ by the result cited in the source; the general case remains open.

334534.title: Vertex-transitive graph power decomposition conjecture
334534.statement: For a finite graph $G$, let $G^n$ be the graph with vertex set $V(G)^n$, in which two vertices are adjacent exactly when they differ in one coordinate and the entries in that coordinate are adjacent in $G$. Let $H$ be an induced subgraph of $G$. **Vertex-transitive graph power decomposition conjecture.** If $G$ is vertex-transitive and every prime factor of $|H|$ divides $|G|$, then there exists a positive integer $n$ such that $G^n$ can be partitioned into induced copies of $H$. This proposes that the hypercube decomposition phenomenon extends to powers of every finite vertex-transitive graph under the stated prime-divisibility condition; the source supplies no resolution.

381197.title: Polynomial recoloring diameter conjecture for planar graphs
381197.statement: Let $G$ be a planar graph and let $k$ be an integer. The $k$-recoloring graph $R_k(G)$ has vertices corresponding to proper $k$-colorings of $G$, with edges joining colorings that differ on one vertex by one color. **Polynomial recoloring diameter conjecture.** For every planar graph $G$ and every integer $k\geq 7$, the graph $R_k(G)$ has polynomial diameter. This would establish a polynomial recoloring bound for planar graphs with at least seven colors; the statement is presented as a question for further work, and no resolution is given here.
